title: Minimizing Total Biharmonic Distance in Large Graphs via Link Recommendation

problem.claim: Minimize total biharmonic distance by adding k nonexistent edges to a given graph G under budget k.

gap.claim: The optimization problem is computationally challenging, and the initial greedy algorithms have cubic time complexity.

contributions.claim: The objective function is monotone but not supermodular.
The paper proposes simple greedy algorithms for minimizing the objective.
Projection, Laplacian solver, and convex hull approximation techniques reduce the algorithms' time complexity from cubic to nearly linear while providing error guarantees.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments on real datasets demonstrate the efficiency and effectiveness of the proposed algorithms.

narrative_sequence.summary: Total biharmonic distance is presented as a metric for network connectivity and robustness.
The paper studies minimizing total biharmonic distance through link recommendation under an edge-addition budget.
The optimization problem is computationally challenging.
The paper characterizes the objective and proposes greedy algorithms with techniques to reduce their computational cost.
Experiments on real datasets report algorithmic efficiency and effectiveness.

source_observation.claim: When an objective is monotone but not supermodular, simple greedy algorithms can still be used, but the abstract does not state a supermodularity-based guarantee.

interpretation.claim: Structural properties of an objective can guide algorithm selection even when standard favorable properties are absent.

application.claim: For graph optimization problems with expensive objective evaluation, combine greedy selection with computational acceleration techniques.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the conditions, approximation bounds, or dataset-dependent limitations of the reported guarantees.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact greedy algorithms or their approximation guarantees.
The abstract does not provide the numerical error bounds, datasets, baselines, or experimental results.
